subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity questions + sizing worksheet
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@heliopay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity questions + sizing worksheet

Hi Liam — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few items we need to size Dedicated for HelioPay's payment reconciliation assistant: 

Recap (from our notes)
- Primary workload: document-to-invoice reconciliation and short Q&A (average 1–3 turns).
- Peak traffic target: you mentioned 120 TPS over a 30–60 minute peak window, but the shape is burstier across business hours.
- Typical prompt lengths: average prompt 350 tokens, average completion 120 tokens; heavy tails up to ~2k tokens for full invoice contexts.
- Concurrency: expected 40–60 concurrent sessions during peak; internal batch jobs layer on top (nightly bulk processing).
- Data sensitivity: PCI-adjacent; preference toward Dedicated (isolated GPU pool) with optional VPC for encryption at rest.

Open questions for sizing (see inline) — answers will help us pick GPU class and pool sizing:
1) Can you confirm the 120 TPS figure is request-level TPS (requests/sec) rather than tokens/sec? If so, what % of those requests are generation vs. embeddings/rerank?
2) Of the 120 TPS, what % do you expect to be short Q&A (<= 200 tokens total) vs. long reconciliation runs (>1k tokens)?
3) For batch/nightly jobs: how many documents per job and approximate average seq length? Do those run during peak or off-peak?
4) Any hard latency SLO for interactive features (p95 target)?

Attached: redwood-dedicated-options.pdf (overview of Dedicated SKUs and network/VPC options) and a short sizing worksheet (heliopay-dedicated-sizing-worksheet.xlsx). Please fill the worksheet with token mix and schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week; I blocked 4 slots on Tue/Wed.

Next steps
- HelioPay: confirm answers to the 4 sizing questions and return the worksheet.
- Redwood: once we have the worksheet, Vivek will simulate cost/latency options across A100/H100 and recommend a 2–3 SKU shortlist.

Thanks — Priya

--

Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity questions + sizing worksheet

Thanks Priya — good writeup. Quick answers inline below:

On Mon, Apr 12, 2026 at 3:10 PM Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm the 120 TPS figure is request-level TPS (requests/sec) rather than tokens/sec? If so, what % of those requests are generation vs. embeddings/rerank?

That 120 TPS is requests/sec. Rough split today is ~80% generation (the assistant) and ~20% embeddings for similarity search/rerank.

> 2) Of the 120 TPS, what % do you expect to be short Q&A (<= 200 tokens total) vs. long reconciliation runs (>1k tokens)?

Estimate: about 65% short Q&A, 25% mid-length (200–800 tokens), and 10% long reconciliation runs (~1–2k tokens).

> 3) For batch/nightly jobs: how many documents per job and approximate average seq length? Do those run during peak or off-peak?

Batch jobs: ~10k documents per job, average seq length around 900 tokens. They run off-peak (2–4am local).

> 4) Any hard latency SLO for interactive features (p95 target)?

Yes — product wants p95 <= 450ms for short Q&A flows. Longer reconciliations can be async.

I'll pass this to Priyanka (ops) to fill the worksheet — expect it back by EOD Wed.

Liam

liam@heliopay.com | +1 (646) 555-0199

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated capacity questions + sizing worksheet

Liam — appreciate the quick answers, super helpful. A few technical clarifications so we size correctly: 

1) Model family: do you have a preferred family (open Llama 2 variants, Falcon, etc.) or are you open to Redwood recommendations? The choice impacts memory profile and token throughput.
2) For the long reconciliation runs (~2k tokens), are you sending them as single contiguous prompts (single-request decode) or streaming across multiple calls?
3) Do you expect KV cache reuse between requests for the same session (i.e., user sessions that send incremental messages), or are most requests independent?

Sizing guidance (what we'll run after worksheet):
- If p95 450ms target for short Q&A, we generally look at H100-class machines for lowest latency at scale, but a mixed pool with A100 or H800 variants can reduce cost while still meeting p95 for mid-length requests.
- For 120 req/s with your token mix, preliminary thumb estimate: 6–10 H100 GPUs (or 10–14 A100 GPUs) dedicated, depending on model and batching strategy. This assumes continuous peak; autoscaling/burst policies will change the commit size.
- For large nightly batches, we recommend scheduling them to dedicated off-peak GPUs or using transient spot capacity in a separate pool to avoid impacting latency-based production pools.

I'll run a quick simulation once the worksheet is back — expect the H100 vs A100 cost/latency delta and a recommended pool configuration (min/max GPUs, per-GPU concurrency targets).

If helpful, we can do a short technical deep-dive (30m) with your infra/ML infra team to walk through KV caching patterns and session stickiness. Priya — do you want me on the follow-up call?

Thanks — Vivek
